info.title: Student Information Service
info.description:
Student Information Service — the registrar's system of record for school structure, class placement and stated grades.

**A blank grade is `null`, never `0`.** Zero is a mark a child can earn; the absence of a mark is not. Every grade field in this API distinguishes the two, and a client that renders `null` as `0%` is reporting a failure that did not happen.

**Class placement is a dated membership, not a property of the student.** A child who moves from 3A to 3B in March is in 3A for Term 1 and 3B for Term 2, and both remain true forever. Ask for a placement *as of* a date or a term; there is no 'current class' field to read.

**Imports are preview-then-commit.** An upload is parsed and validated into a batch with a per-row outcome, and nothing is written until that batch is committed. One malformed row is reported as one rejected row — it never discards the rows around it.

**Codes are immutable; labels are not.** A class is identified by its code for its whole life, so renaming '3A' to 'Falcons' changes a label and detaches no student and no grade. Every nameable thing carries both an Arabic and an English name.

Grades here are stated figures, reported exactly as the school recorded them. This service does not average, weight, or drop the lowest.

Both lists in one body so the two selects on a structure screen cannot be fetched a moment apart and disagree.

`school` narrows both to one school and is optional: without it the years of every school are returned and `year_levels` is empty, because a ladder only means something inside a school and merging several would put two branches' `Y1` side by side with nothing to tell them apart. The school picker itself is the caller that omits it.

post.summary: Move one child to another class
post.description: One transaction: the open placement is closed the day before `on_date` and a new one opens on it. Two separate calls would leave a window in which the child is in no class at all, and a marks upload landing in that window rejects every one of her rows for having no placement. Her marks in the old class stay filed under the old class — that is the point of the invariant.

put.summary: Record the register for one class on one day
put.description:
Idempotent: saving the same morning twice corrects the marks rather than writing a second set beside them, because a day holds one statement per child.

PUT rather than POST for that reason — the request states what the register *is* for that day, and repeating it changes nothing. Children absent from `entries` are left untouched, so a partial register can be saved and finished later.

A child who was not in this class on this day is refused with her number in the message: that is a stale screen or the wrong class, and writing it would file her attendance under a room she had already left.

get.summary: One child's attendance over a range
get.description:
Oldest first, with counts. Both `from` and `to` are inclusive and both are optional; omitting them returns everything on file.

The counts carry `recorded` — the number of days a mark exists for — and no rate. A percentage needs a denominator, and the only one this service can state honestly is the days somebody actually took the register.

code.title: Code
code.description: Academic year code. Globally unique, so it names one year at one school — two branches cannot both use `2025-2026` and must distinguish them.

school_code.title: School Code
school_code.description: The school this year belongs to. Must already exist.

ends_on.title: Ends On
ends_on.description: Last day of the year, inclusive.

is_current.title: Is Current
is_current.description: Make this the working year. Defaults true: a registrar creating a year almost always means the one they are about to build.

AcademicYearIn.title: AcademicYearIn
AcademicYearIn.description:
Create or relabel one school year.

Upsert rather than insert-only, for the same reason as terms and subjects: `code` is
identity and the names are labels, so correcting a spelling must not create a second
year beside the one every class already points at.

school_code.title: School Code
school_code.description: The school this year belongs to. Year codes are globally unique, so a code names one year at one school — this says which.

restriction_note.title: Restriction Note
restriction_note.description: Why. Recorded whichever way the flag went, so a later reader can tell a deliberate restriction from a default that was never revisited.

AccessIn.title: AccessIn
AccessIn.description: A custody decision, applied to one link.

label.title: Label
label.description: Which system holds this key. A key nobody can attribute is a key nobody dares revoke.

scope.description: `registrar` writes, `reader` reads. Checked by exact equality: a registrar key is refused by reader-only routes and vice versa.

expires_in_days.title: Expires In Days
expires_in_days.description: Omit for a key that must be revoked deliberately rather than expiring under someone at 3am.

prefix.title: Prefix
prefix.description: The public handle. Appears in logs and audit rows so a human can point at one key and revoke it.

api_key.title: Api Key
api_key.description: The secret, shown exactly once. Store it now; the service keeps only a hash and cannot show it again.

ApiKeyOut.title: ApiKeyOut
ApiKeyOut.description: The minted key. `api_key` appears here and is never retrievable again.

note.title: Note
note.description: Required for `excused`: an excused absence with no reason on file cannot be told apart from an ordinary one marked by mistake.

AttendanceEntryIn.title: AttendanceEntryIn
AttendanceEntryIn.description: One child's state for the day, and why if it needs one.

on_date.title: On Date
on_date.description: The day this register is a statement about. Echoed because `on` defaults to today, and a caller who meant last Friday must be able to see that it did not.

size.title: Size
size.description: Children placed in this class on that day.

unmarked.title: Unmarked
unmarked.description: How many of them nobody marked. Reported separately and never folded into the counts, so an unfinished register cannot read as a finished one.

is_complete.title: Is Complete
is_complete.description: Whether every child has a mark — not whether they were present.

as_of.title: As Of
as_of.description: The day this register answers for. Echoed because `on` defaults to today, and a caller who meant last term must be able to see that it did.

code.title: Code
code.description: Unique within the academic year, and immutable once created. Renaming is a label change through PATCH; the code is identity.

year_level_code.title: Year Level Code
year_level_code.description: The rung this section sits on. Must already exist.

capacity.title: Capacity
capacity.description: Places in the room. `null` means nobody has stated one, which is not the same as `0` — a capacity of zero is a section that admits nobody, and a registrar can legitimately mean it.

ClassSectionIn.title: ClassSectionIn
ClassSectionIn.description: One class section, in one academic year, on one year level.

capacity.title: Capacity
capacity.description: `null` means no stated limit. It is not 0 — a capacity of 0 is a section that admits nobody, which a registrar closing a class may mean.

ClassSectionPatch.title: ClassSectionPatch
ClassSectionPatch.description:
Labels only. There is deliberately no `code` and no `year_level_code` here.

Moving a class to another rung or renaming its code would carry every enrolment and
every mark with it, under a class the children were never in. Both are new sections
plus a roster change, and neither is an edit.

field.title: Field
field.description: Which input caused it, when a single one did. Lets a UI highlight the cell rather than reddening the whole form.

ErrorDetail.title: ErrorDetail
ErrorDetail.description:
The body of a refusal: a code to branch on, a sentence to show, a cell to blame.

`code` is the contract and `message` is prose — a client that branches on the wording
breaks the first time somebody translates it into Arabic, which this school will do.

ErrorOut.title: ErrorOut
ErrorOut.description: Every failure this service returns, nested under FastAPI's own `detail` key.

classes_by_year.title: Classes By Year
classes_by_year.description: Year level code to section count, e.g. `{"Y1": 3, "Y2": 5}`. Key order is creation order.

allow_new_convention.title: Allow New Convention
allow_new_convention.description: Set only to build a second ladder beside the codes already on file. The default refusal exists because a mismatched template generates a full set of empty classes that reports as a success and strands every existing enrolment.

GenerateStructureIn.title: GenerateStructureIn
GenerateStructureIn.description:
Either uniform (`year_count` + `classes_per_year`) or explicit (`classes_by_year`).

Every template is optional and omitted fields keep the command's own defaults; sending
an explicit `null` is treated as "not stated" for the same reason, so a client that
serialises its whole form does not blank a template into a crash.

created.title: Created
created.description: `false` is a success, not a skip: generation is idempotent, so a re-run reports what was already there.

subject_name_ar.title: Subject Name Ar
subject_name_ar.description: Empty when the subject row could not be loaded. The line is still returned — a report card that quietly drops a line is one nobody can tell is incomplete.

is_graded.title: Is Graded
is_graded.description: The supported way to ask whether a mark exists. `false` means the subject has not been marked yet; it does not mean zero.

percentage.title: Percentage
percentage.description: `null` when not graded yet — never 0. A stated 0 is a mark the child earned and is returned as `0.0` with `is_graded: true`.

points.title: Points
points.description: The raw figure the teacher wrote, when the sheet stated one. Never recomputed from `percentage`, and `percentage` is never recomputed from it.

class_code.title: Class Code
class_code.description: The class this mark was earned in, carried on the grade itself so a later transfer cannot reprint it under a room the child had not yet entered.

GradeLineOut.title: GradeLineOut
GradeLineOut.description: One line of a report card: a subject, and the figure the school stated for it.

GuardianChildOut.title: GuardianChildOut
GuardianChildOut.description: One child a guardian is responsible for.

phone.title: Phone
phone.description: Her identifying number, in E.164. Normalised on the way in, so the same parent typed three ways in three uploads appears once.

phones.title: Phones
phones.description: Every number that reaches her, this one first.

full_name_ar.title: Full Name Ar
full_name_ar.description: Empty when the guardian row could not be loaded. The link is still listed: a contact list that is quietly one adult short is worse than one showing a number without a name — the number still reaches somebody.

relationship_type.description: The closed vocabulary, for counting and filtering.

relationship_label.title: Relationship Label
relationship_label.description: What the registrar actually typed — 'big brother' — kept verbatim beside the bucketed type.

can_view_records.title: Can View Records
can_view_records.description: Whether this adult may read the child's academic records. Separate from the link existing: an emergency contact barred by a court order stays on file and reads nothing.

restriction_note.title: Restriction Note
restriction_note.description: Why access was restricted. For the registrar and an audit; never rendered to a parent.

GuardianOut.title: GuardianOut
GuardianOut.description: One adult on a child's contact list, and what she is to that child.

public_id.title: Public Id
public_id.description: Opaque and permanent. This is what another service stores to refer to her later, so that it never has to keep her phone number.

GuardianRefOut.title: GuardianRefOut
GuardianRefOut.description: A guardian named by her stable handle. Deliberately carries no phone number back.

checked_at.title: Checked At
checked_at.description: When this process answered, in UTC. A stale value in a proxied response is how a cached health page is spotted.

HealthOut.title: HealthOut
HealthOut.description: What a probe reads. Deliberately says nothing about stored data.

ImportCommitOut.title: ImportCommitOut
ImportCommitOut.description:
What was actually written, row by row — not assumed to match the preview.

A row that previewed `ok` can commit as `changed_since_preview` because somebody else
edited the same child in between, so this is a fresh account rather than an echo.

ImportKind.title: ImportKind
ImportKind.description:
What a file is claiming to be. Chosen by the caller, never sniffed.

A `StrEnum` because these values are persisted, put in URLs and shown in JSON; an
`IntEnum` would store `0` and `1` and make the database unreadable to the person
debugging an import at 7am, while a bare `str` would let `"rosters"` reach the
parser registry and fail as "unknown kind" three layers from the typo.

Kind is *not* inferred from the file's columns. A grades sheet whose header row was
edited can look like a roster, and guessing wrong means writing enrolments from a
file of marks.

batch_id.title: Batch Id
batch_id.description: Name this in the commit call; do not re-upload.

expires_at.title: Expires At
expires_at.description: After this the batch cannot be committed and the file must be uploaded again — a preview taken against last week's class list must not be applied to today's.

totals.title: Totals
totals.description: Counts per row code, omitting codes that did not occur. These are the filter chips above the table.

ImportPreviewOut.title: ImportPreviewOut
ImportPreviewOut.description: What the registrar reads *before* anything is written.

status.description: Derived against the clock on read, so a preview past its TTL reports `expired` rather than offering a commit that will fail.

actor.title: Actor
actor.description: The prefix of the key that uploaded the file.

counts.title: Counts
counts.description: Rows per outcome, with every outcome present so a zero is explicit.

total.title: Total
total.description: Rows matching the filter, not the size of this page.

limit.title: Limit
limit.description: The window actually applied. A larger request is clamped rather than refused, so this may be smaller than the one asked for.

ImportReportOut.title: ImportReportOut
ImportReportOut.description: A batch and one page of its rows.

outcome.description: Whether anything was, or would be, written.

code.title: Code
code.description: Why. Finer-grained than `outcome` and stable on the wire.

ImportRowOut.title: ImportRowOut
ImportRowOut.description: One stored row of a batch: its fate, its diagnosis, and the cells it came from.

ImportStatus.title: ImportStatus
ImportStatus.description: Where a batch is in the two-step flow. Only `PREVIEWED` may be committed.

ends_on.title: Ends On
ends_on.description: Her last day in the class she is currently in — not the day after.

starts_on.title: Starts On
starts_on.description: Her first day in this class.

ends_on.title: Ends On
ends_on.description: Her **last day** in the class, not the day after. `null` opens the placement — she is in this class now and no end has been decided.

PlacementIn.title: PlacementIn
PlacementIn.description: Put a child in a class from a date.

state.title: State
state.description: present / absent / late / excused, or **null** when nobody marked her. Null is not absent: rendering it as either states a fact the school did not.

RegisterLineOut.title: RegisterLineOut
RegisterLineOut.description: One child on a day's register.

RelationshipType.title: RelationshipType
RelationshipType.description:
Who a guardian is to a child. A closed vocabulary, with the words kept beside it.

Closed because this is the half that gets *counted*: "how many mothers are on file",
"show me every child whose only contact is a sibling". Free text cannot be counted —
"mother", "Mother" and "الأم" tally as three — and it cannot be translated, since a
string typed into a spreadsheet appears in no translation table the UI owns.

The cost of a closed list is that it cannot describe every family, which is what
`StudentGuardian.relationship_label` is for: "big brother" buckets to `SIBLING` here
and survives verbatim there. Degrading an unrecognised word to `OTHER` is therefore
lossless, which is why it is safe — unlike guessing at an unfamiliar *grade*, where
the guess would replace a fact nobody could recover.

phone.title: Phone
phone.description: The number in international form, e.g. +201001234567, or in the school's national form. Normalised here, so a caller holding whatever a parent typed does not have to know the rules.

default_country_code.title: Default Country Code
default_country_code.description: Applied only to a number given in national form. A number carrying its own + prefix ignores this entirely.

ResolveIn.title: ResolveIn
ResolveIn.description: A number to look up. In a body, never a path — see the route's own docstring.

full_name_ar.title: Full Name Ar
full_name_ar.description: Empty when the student row could not be loaded. The placement is still listed: a register that is quietly one child short is worse than one showing a number without a name.

ends_on.title: Ends On
ends_on.description: Her **last day** in the class, not the day after. `null` means the placement is open — she is in this class now and no end has been decided.

RosterEntryOut.title: RosterEntryOut
RosterEntryOut.description: One child on the register, with the placement window she is listed under.

RowCode.title: RowCode
RowCode.description:
Every outcome a single import row can have. Closed on purpose — see the module docstring.

`StrEnum` so the member *is* its wire value: `RowCode.OK == "ok"` holds, JSON
encoding needs no custom hook, and a stored batch read back from the database
reconstructs by value. The cost is that a typo in a comparison against a bare string
is silently false, which is why services should compare against members.

RowOutcome.title: RowOutcome
RowOutcome.description:
What happened, or would happen, to one row.

The distinction between `CREATED`, `UPDATED` and `UNCHANGED` is what makes a preview
worth reading: a registrar re-uploading a corrected file needs to see that 200 rows
are unchanged and 3 are updated. Collapsing those into "ok" hides the three rows
that are the entire reason for the upload.

`SKIPPED` is deliberately separate from `REJECTED`. A skipped row is one the file
asked to be ignored — a blank line, a totals row — and it is not a defect the
registrar has to fix. Counting it as a rejection makes a clean file look broken.

line.title: Line
line.description: The number in Excel's own gutter, 1-based and counting the header, so 'row 12 is wrong' points at row 12 on the registrar's screen.

code.description: A closed vocabulary, safe to filter and count on. `ok` is the only non-failure.

message.title: Message
message.description: Prose for a human. Nothing may branch on its wording — it is translated.

field.title: Field
field.description: Which column failed, when a single one did.

payload.title: Payload
payload.description: The row's identifying cells, so a table can be rendered without holding the original file.

RowOutcomeOut.title: RowOutcomeOut
RowOutcomeOut.description: What happened, or would happen, to one line of the uploaded file.

code.title: Code
code.description: Immutable identity. Every year and rung in the school points at it.

is_active.title: Is Active
is_active.description: Set false to close a branch. Nothing is deleted: the registers taken and marks stated in the years it ran are still true, and the database refuses a delete while any year or rung points at it.

Scope.title: Scope
Scope.description:
What a key may do. Two levels, checked by exact equality.

`StrEnum` so the member serialises to its own literal (`"registrar"`, `"reader"`) in
JSON and in a database column without a translation table that can drift from the
enum it mirrors.

current_academic_year_code.title: Current Academic Year Code
current_academic_year_code.description: `null` until a registrar has marked one current; never guessed from today's date.

StructureYearsOut.title: StructureYearsOut
StructureYearsOut.description: Both ladders at once — see the module note on why this is one route.

to_date.title: To Date
to_date.description: Both bounds inclusive, and echoed: a count of absences means nothing without the window it was counted over.

class_code.title: Class Code
class_code.description: The class she was in that day — stored on the mark, not resolved now, so a transfer in March leaves October's register saying 3A.

student_number.title: Student Number
student_number.description: The school's own identifier, and the key every mark and guardian link points at. Immutable — correcting a mistyped number is a new student plus a roster fix, not an edit, because the old number may already carry marks.

is_active.title: Is Active
is_active.description: False once the child has left the school. She keeps her marks, her placements and her guardians; she stops appearing in the pickers.

date_of_birth.title: Date Of Birth
date_of_birth.description: Stated, never derived — and there is no age field anywhere in this API, because an age is right for one year and silently wrong afterwards. A date in the future is refused.

contact_phone.title: Contact Phone
contact_phone.description: The child's own number, which is **not** her guardian's. Guardian numbers live under `/students/{student_number}/guardians`, where the permission to be told about her marks lives with them.

StudentIn.title: StudentIn
StudentIn.description: A child's own record: her number and how her name is written.

age.title: Age
age.description: Her age in whole years **as of the day this response was built**, computed from `date_of_birth` and never stored. `null` when no birth date is on file — which is not the same as nought, exactly as a blank mark is not a zero.

StudentPatch.title: StudentPatch
StudentPatch.description:
A correction. Every field optional; omitted means leave it alone.

`student_number` is absent by design. It is in the path, and it is identity.

query.title: Query
query.description: Echoed, so a stale response is recognisable as stale.

class_code.title: Class Code
class_code.description: The class she was in *for this term*. `null` means no placement covered it — she had left, or had not yet joined — and is deliberately distinguishable from her current class.

subject_count.title: Subject Count
subject_count.description: Subjects with a row this term, graded or not.

graded_count.title: Graded Count
graded_count.description: Subjects carrying a stated figure. The remainder are awaiting a mark, not scoring zero. This is a count, not a score.

StudentTermGradesOut.title: StudentTermGradesOut
StudentTermGradesOut.description: One child, one term, the marks as stated. No aggregate of any kind.

academic_year_code.title: Academic Year Code
academic_year_code.description: The year that teaches this subject. Part of its identity, not a tag.

is_active.title: Is Active
is_active.description: Retire a subject with `false` rather than deleting it; marks already stated against it must keep resolving, or that year's report card loses a heading.

SubjectIn.title: SubjectIn
SubjectIn.description:
One subject as one academic year teaches it.

`academic_year_code` is required and is half of the subject's identity. The same code
in two years is two subjects, so posting `MATH` for 2026-2027 creates a row rather than
colliding with the `MATH` of 2025-2026 — and a mark stated against one of them is not a
mark on the other.

TakeRegisterIn.title: TakeRegisterIn
TakeRegisterIn.description:
A day's register for one class.

Children left out of `entries` are **left alone**, not marked. Taking the register for
the twelve children present so far must not silently mark the other twenty-eight absent,
and a second save later in the morning is a correction of the names it carries and a
no-op for the rest.

recorded.title: Recorded
recorded.description: Days a mark exists for — the only honest denominator this service has. It is not the number of school days: no calendar is held here, so an unmarked Tuesday cannot be told from a holiday.

in_the_room.title: In The Room
in_the_room.description: Present plus late: days she was actually there.

away.title: Away
away.description: Absent plus excused: days she was not.

TallyOut.title: TallyOut
TallyOut.description: Counts, and the number of days they were counted over. Never a rate.

sequence.title: Sequence
sequence.description: Chronological order without parsing the code, which schools format freely.

is_closed.title: Is Closed
is_closed.description: Stated by a human, never derived from `ends_on`: a school enters late marks for a week after a term ends.

on_date.title: On Date
on_date.description: Her first day in the new class. The old placement is closed the day before, so no single day belongs to two classes.

TransferIn.title: TransferIn
TransferIn.description: Move a child to another class in the same year, from a date.

closed.description: The placement that ended, or `null` when the child had none open — which is a first placement rather than a transfer, and is not an error.

code.title: Code
code.description: Unique within the school, not globally: `Y1` exists at every branch.

display_order.title: Display Order
display_order.description: Order within the stage. Stated, not derived from the code: `Y10` sorts before `Y9` as text.

stage.title: Stage
stage.description: garden / primary / preparatory / secondary, or `unspecified`. Grouping only — no rule anywhere depends on it. An unrecognised value is refused rather than silently treated as unspecified.

YearLevelIn.title: YearLevelIn
YearLevelIn.description: Add or relabel one rung of one school's ladder.

school_code.title: School Code
school_code.description: Rung codes are unique *within* a school, because 'Year 1' exists at every branch. This is the half of the identity the code does not carry.

stage.title: Stage
stage.description: garden / primary / preparatory / secondary, or `unspecified`. A label for grouping a long ladder on screen; it carries no rules.

display_order.title: Display Order
display_order.description: Stated order, not code order: `Y10` sorts before `Y9` as text, so a school with ten rungs prints its ladder scrambled without this.
